Exparte *J U D G M E N T

* This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 25.12.2021 at about 11.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Registration No. KA10EB 5820, on the left side of the road, near Achgal Circle, Opp. to Sampath Godown, Kollegala Town,
Chamarajanagar District, at that time, one Lorry bearing Registration No.KA01AE4824, came Mr. Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133660/
1 with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, and dashed against the motor cycle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital,
Kollegala, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and took treatment for accidental injuries.

It is stated that, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards hospitalization, medical treatment,
conveyance and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years, self employed and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he was permanently disabled and unable to do his work, as he was doing earlier.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA01AE4824.
In this regard, case has been registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Kollegala Town Police station as per Crime No.209/2021.
As such, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
6. After service of the notice of this petition, the respondent has not made an effort to appear before the court, and remained absent.
Hence, he was placed exparte as per the order of this court dated 19.01.2023.
Thereafter, matter was set down for evidence.

7. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner by name Shri Ravi N., son of Nataraju, during the course of evidence, placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examinationinchief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of his evidence, 10 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, for consideration.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW2.
At the time of his evidence, 2 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P11 to Ex.P12, for consideration.
8. Heard the argument.
And perused the materials available on record.
9. Consequently, following points would arise for final determination of the case.

They are as follows;
POINTS 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA01 AE4824 on 25.12.2021 at about 11.00 a.m. near Achgal Circle, Opp. to Sampath Godown, Kollegala Town, Chamarajanagar District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?
From whom?

2 3.

10. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid points are as follows:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S POINT NO.1:
11.
It is the case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Lorry bearing registration No.KA13C 8995, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
12. On the other hand, the respondent remained as silent spectator, without challenging the case of the petitioner.
On going through the above points, burden is on the petitioner, to prove the same, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
To discharge the burden lies on the petitioner by name Ravi N., relied on his affidavit evidence and examined as PW1.
At the time of his evidence 10 documents got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
Since the respondent placed exparte, burden is more on the petitioner, to prove the above point.
It is also abundant duty of the court to scrutinize the evidence available on record carefully in order to come to the fair conclusion.

13. In the affidavit evidence, reiterated all the averments made in the main petition, about the accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is necessary to appreciate the evidence in toto, in order to come to the conclusion, whether there is a direct nexus between the accident and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, which caused injuries to the petitioner.
14. The petitioner herein, to demonstrate his assertions, relied on the documentary evidence.
Among them Ex.P1, first information report, goes to show that, alleged accident had taken place on 25.12.2021.
On the same day one Chethan gave first information against the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA13C8995.
The complainant is none other than an eye witness to the accident.

On the basis of the said information, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC and under section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act.

In column No.10 of Ex.P1 and the, narration made in the complaint, about the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle,
remained unquestioned.
There is no delay in giving first information about the accident.

If at all, the driver of the offending vehicle was innocent, what prevented to him to question the recitals of Ex.P1 & Ex.P2, well in time before the competent court of law or why he has not made an effort to file complaint against the driver of the defending vehicle.
15.

Added to this, the recitals of the spot mahazar and seizure mahazars marked at Ex.P3 to Ex.P5,
go to show that, after setting criminal law in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, the investigation officer visited the spot and prepared mahazar process, in presence of panch witnesses,
Mr. Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133660/
3 clearly speak about involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

entities.text: Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the report of the IMV inspector, marked at Ex.P6, with respect to the damages, remained unquestioned.
And as per the opinion of the inspector, accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.
Another document wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 depict that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury.
All these material documents remained unshaken.

16. Ultimately, on perusal of the final report submitted by the investigation officer speaks that, on the allegation made in the column N.17, of the charge sheet, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle by name, Muthukooru Prasad @ Nagaprasad, Son of Late Rangaiah,
and R.Ramanjaneya Reddy, son of B.R.Subbareddy, who are the driver and owner of the offending vehicle, by showing them, as accused No.1 and 2, filed chargesheet, on the allegation that, the accused No.1 had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC and also Section 3(1) r/w.181 of M.V. Act.
And also alleging that, the accused No.2 has committed offences punishable u/s. 3(1), r/w. 192, 196, 5(1) and 180 of IMV Act.

It is the main allegation forth coming in column No.4 of the charge sheet that, accused No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle was not having permit, insurance policy, handed over the offending vehicle, to the driver, who had no valid driving license as on the date of the alleged accident.
And due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

17. Overall appreciation of the prosecution papers furnished by the petitioner, in the absence of contra materials, there is no hurdle to say that, Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are substantive piece of evidence in connection with the above point, and they are conclusive proof in connection with the fact in issue.
Evidence of PW1 placed through affidavit evidence and documentary evidence
remained unimpeached by placing rebuttal evidence by the respondent.
As such, adverse inference can be drawn against them as contemplated under law.

18. In the light of the evidence placed on record, by way of affidavit and the documentary evidence,
speak that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence,
to prove the above point to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA01AE4824.

Hence,
without making many discussions on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Point No.1, in the Affirmative.

POINT NO.2 :
19.
This point is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

20. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the prepositions laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Mr. Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133660/
4 Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."
21.

In the light of the preposition laid down in the above case, it is also relevant to note that, "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.

But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation".
22.
In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, in the accident, has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P7.

The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries:
1. Swelling and tenderness, abrasion in the hip region.
2. Swelling and tenderness, abrasion in the left ankle.
Xray of pelvis revealed fracture of 3rd and 4th segments of coccyx with sacrococcygeal separation.
23.
In connection with the above injuries, doctor opined that, the said injuries are simple and grievous in nature.
Apart from this, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P9.
In addition to this, placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2, and placed clinical note & xray as per Ex.P11 & Ex.P12.
On going through the discharge summary of Government hospital, Kollegala marked at Ex.P9 disclose that, the petitioner had taken the treatment as an inpatient from 25.12.2021 to 06.01.2022.

For having taken the note of the nature of the injuries sustained by him,
and by keeping in mind about his sufferings during the said period of treatment, in connection with the grievous injuries, and also, by taking in to consideration of the mode of treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.35,000/ towards pain and suffering.
24. Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period, and rest period.
In the petition, he had stated that, he was self employed and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
To substantiate the said fact, there is no iota of documents to show that, the petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/ per month, prior to the accident.
On the other hand, it is to be noted that, the injuries sustained by him are simple as well as grievous in nature, as per the wound certificate.
On going through the discharge summary of Government hospital, Kollegala marked at Ex.P9 disclose that, the petitioner had taken the treatment as an inpatient from 25.12.2021 to 06.01.2022.

Hence,
definitely there was some difficulty to him, during the period of treatment and followup treatment,
Mr. Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133660/
5

entities.text: Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for fifteen days.
Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,500/ towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.
25. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained grievous injuries.
On going through the discharge summary of Government hospital, Kollegala, the petitioner took conservative treatment in the said hospital from 25.12.2021 to 06.01.2022.
Later on, he was advised for further treatment.
As such, during the period of treatment, and further treatment, the petitioner could have spent some amount towards traveling, food and nourishment.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/ towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
26. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he has sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence, along with the wound certificate, and other medical documents.
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him, as per Ex.P7, goes to show that, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
To substantiate this, the petitioner has placed, wound certificate for consideration.

Apart from this, the petitioner had placed the evidence of the doctor by name Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2.
27.
In the evidence of this material witness PW2, deposed that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained the above said injuries.

In this regard, the petitioner was treated at General hospital,
Kollegal.
At the time of diagnosis, found fracture of 3rd and 4th segments of coccyx with sacrococcygeal separation and he was treated conservatively.
At the time of examination of this witness, he found that, the petitioner walks with pain and limping, tenderness over coccyx with sacrcoccygeal junction.
Apart from this on the basis of xray taken on 16.03.2023, noticed sacrcoccygeal separation.
After assessing the disabilities, on various aspects, came to the conclusion that, total disability to the whole body at 10%.

In support of the evidence of PW2 produced Ex.P11 &
Ex.P12 for consideration.
28. Over all appreciation of the medical documentary evidence, along with the evidence of PW2 in toto, I am of the view that, whole body disability expressed by the PW2, seems little bit exorbitant.
The petitioner herein, had sustained one simple injury and one grievous injury.
And he took conservative treatment.

Hence, it is apt to take the whole body disability of the petitioner as 7%
instead of 10%.
Accordingly, it is apt to take the percentage of disability of the whole body of the petitioner as 7%, the same will meets the ends of justice.
29. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 23 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P10.
On going through the said documents, pertaining to the petitioner, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 01.01.1998.
The accident occurred on 25.12.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is considered as 23 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

Mr. Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133660/
6 30.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examinationinchief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was self employed and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
In support of his avocation, and definite income per month, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.

But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously,
by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

Hence, by keeping in mind about the year of the institution of this case, and also, as per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/ for the year 2021.

31. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,000 X 12 X 18 X 7/100= Rs.2,26,800/.
32.

Next factual aspect loss of amenities is concerned, due to the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and discharge summaries, definitely, and on appreciation of the evidence of the PW2 in toto, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work.
By taking into consideration of all these aspects, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/ towards loss of amenities.
33. In so far as the future medical expenses are concerned, the PW2, in his evidence, not stated anything about the future medical expenses.
And also, the petitioner has not produced any documents, in this regard.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitle for compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

34. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in toto, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  (in Rupees)
 1. Pain and Suffering 35,000.00  2. Loss of income during laid 7,500.00  up period and rest period  3. Attendant, Nourishment 10,000.00  and Conveyance Charges
4 . Loss of future income 2,26,800.00  5. Loss of Amenities 20,000.00  6. Loss of future medical NIL  expenses.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for Mr. Ravi N vs Mr. R. Ramanjaneya Reddy on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133660/
7 compensation of Rs.2,99,300/(Rupees Two lakhs ninety nine thousand three hundred only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.
Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
36.
As regards the liability is concerned, in the case on hand, accident has not been seriously disputed by the other side.

And the evidence given by the petitioner that,
due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, Lorry bearing registration No.KA01 AE4824, remained unshaken.
37. On the other hand, the respondent remained silent without challenging the case of the petitioner.

On going through the police papers placed by the petitioner, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was not in force, and also the driver had no driving license.

Hence,
the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle cannot escape from his liability to pay compensation determined by this court.
Since, master held liable, he has to pay compensation.
38. However, the respondent, being the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle, has to satisfy the award with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the point No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

POINT NO.3:
39.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R* The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of MV Act, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,99,300/(Rupees Two lakhs ninety nine thousand three hundred only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the date of deposit.

The respondent is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition, till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.

On going through the police papers placed by the petitioner, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was not in force, and also the driver had no driving license.
Hence,
the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle cannot escape from his liability to pay compensation determined by this court.
Since, master held liable, he has to pay compensation.
